ai_summary: Great Britain’s electricity network is currently managing substantial renewable volumes, with total GB wind output standing at 9.5 GW, including an estimated Scottish wind output of 3.8 GW. Operating at 37.6% of installed Scottish wind capacity, this northern generation drives Scottish carbon intensity down to 0 gCO2/kWh, compared to 88 gCO2/kWh GB-wide. However, significant grid transmission bottlenecks prevent this clean power from flowing south to demand centres. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 27.6 GWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, accumulating a direct constraint cost of about £818,877. To compensate for this stranded zero-carbon power, an estimated 5,241,720 m3 of fossil gas was burned elsewhere on the grid, emitting 9,656 tonnes of CO2. Annualising today's constraint expenditure indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £299 million, which adds an estimated increase of approximately £1/MWh to consumer electricity invoices across the UK. Eliminating these transmission boundaries through grid reinforcement remains vital to reducing consumer bill surcharges, cutting balancing expenditure, and preventing avoidable fossil-fuel emissions.
